==English== ===Alternative forms=== * {{alter|en|meve||12th to 16th centuries}} * {{alter|en|mieve|mooue|moove||obsolete}} ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:moven>>|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|moven}}, {{m|enm|moeven}}, {{m|enm|meven}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro-nor|mover}}, {{m|fro|moveir}} and {{der|en|fro|mouver}}, {{m|fro|moveir|t=to move}} (compare modern French {{m|fr|mouvoir}} from Old French {{m|fro|movoir}}), from {{der|en|la|moveō|movēre|t=move; change, exchange, go in or out, quit}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*m(y)ewh₁-|t=to move, drive}}. Cognate with {{cog|lt|mauti|t=to push on, rush}}, {{cog|sa|मीवति|tr=mī́vati|t=pushes, presses, moves}}, {{cog|dum|mouwe|t=sleeve}}. Largely displaced native {{noncog|en|stir}}, from {{noncog|enm|stiren}}, {{m|enm|sturien}}, from {{noncog|ang|styrian}}. See also {{noncog|ang|hrēran}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|mo͞ov}}, {{IPA|en|/muːv/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-move.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|uːv|s=1}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[change]] [[place]] or [[posture]]; to [[go]], in any manner, from one place or [[position]] to another. #: {{syn|en|shift|stir|Thesaurus:move|Thesaurus:position}} #: {{ux|en|A ship '''moves''' rapidly.}} #: {{ux|en|I was sitting on the sofa for a long time, feeling too lazy to '''move'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1780|author=w:William Cowper|title=Twenty-ſix Letters on Religious Subjects{{...}} To which are added Hymns{{...}}|edition=4th|chapter={{w|God Moves in a Mysterious Way|Light Shining out of Darkneſs}}|url=https://books.google.co.nz/books?id=rKhVAAAAcAAJ|page=252|text={{smallcaps|God}} '''moves''' in a myſterious way, / His wonders to perform; / He plants his footſteps in the ſea, / And rides upon the ſtorm.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1839|author=Denison Olmsted|title=A Compendium of Astronomy|page=95 |passage=Secondly, When a body is once in motion it will continue to '''move''' forever, unless something stops it. When a ball is struck on the surface of the earth, the friction of the earth and the resistance of the air soon stop its motion.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[act]]; to take [[action]]; to begin to act #: {{syn|en|get moving|stir|take action}} #: {{ux|en|to '''move''' in a matter}} #: {{ux|en|Come on guys, let's '''move''': there's work to do!}} # {{senseid|en|to change residence}}{{lb|en|intransitive}} To change [[residence]], for example from one house, town, or state, to another; to go and live at another place; similarly to change the location of another establishment such as a business. See also [[move out]] and [[move in]]. #: {{syn|en|flit|move house|remove|shift}} #: {{ux|en|I decided to '''move''' to the country for a more peaceful life.}} #: {{ux|en|They '''moved''' closer to work to cut down commuting time.}} #: {{ux|en|I'm '''moving''' next week but I don't have anything packed yet.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1986|author=Wen-shun Chi|chapter={{w|Chen Duxiu|Ch’en Tu-hsiu}} (1879-1942)|title=Ideological Conflicts in Modern China: Democracy and Authoritarianism|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C_6fpZJIGrYC|year_published=1992|ISBN=1-56000-608-0|LCCN=92-3314|OCLC=25202944|page=202|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=C_6fpZJIGrYC&pg=PA202|text=He then '''moved''' from Nanking to Wuhan and finally to Chungking, but when his health deteriorated, he went to Chiang-chin, a small village near Chungking, for recuperation. There he died on 27 March 1942.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To transport (an item) as part of changing residences. #: {{ux|en|Before my lease ended, I gave away my old sofa because I didn't want to '''move''' it.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|ergative}} To cause to change place or posture in any manner; to set in [[motion]]; to [[carry]], [[convey]], [[draw]], or [[push]] from one place to another #: {{syn|en|drive|impel|propel|stir}} #: {{ux|en|The waves '''moved''' the boat up and down.}} #: {{ux|en|The horse '''moves''' a carriage.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|chess|board games}} To [[transfer]] (a piece) from one [[space]] or position on the [[board]] to another. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:chess move}} #: {{ux|en|She '''moved''' the queen closer to the centre of the board.}} #: {{ux|en|He rolled a 5 and '''moved''' his counter to Boardwalk, the most expensive property on the Monopoly board.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[excite]] to action by the presentation of [[motive]]s; to [[rouse]] by [[representation]], [[persuasion]], or [[appeal]]; to [[influence]]. #: {{syn|en|entice|induce|inveigle|persuade|sway}} #: {{ux|en|This song '''moves''' me to dance.}} #* {{RQ:Knolles Turkes|passage=Seducer of the People, not '''moved''' with the Piety of his Life}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Aeneis|7|passage=No female arts his mind could '''move'''.}} # {{senseid|en|affect emotionally}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To [[arouse]] the [[feeling]]s or [[passion]]s of; especially, to excite to [[tenderness]] or [[compassion]], to excite (for example, an [[emotion]]). #: {{syn|en|affect|excite|touch|trouble}} #: {{ux|en|That book really '''moved''' me.}} #* {{RQ:King James Version|book=Matthew|chapter=9|verse=36|passage=When he saw the multitudes, he was '''moved''' with compassion on them.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} To [[propose]]; to [[recommend]]; specifically, to propose formally for [[consideration]] and [[determination]], in a [[deliberative]] [[assembly]]; to [[submit]] #: {{ux|en|I '''move''' to repeal the rule regarding obligatory school uniform.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1905|author=w:Livy|translator=Canon Roberts|title=From the Founding of the City|section=Book 38 |passage=Two days were thus wasted in the quarrel between the consuls. It was clear that while Faminius was present no decision could be arrived at. Owing to Flaminius' absence through illness, Aemilius seized the opportunity to '''move''' a resolution which the senate adopted. Its purport was that the Ambracians should have all their property restored to them; they should be free to live under their own laws; they should impose such harbour dues and other imposts by land and sea as they desired, provided that the Romans and their Italian allies were exempt.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Much Ado About Nothing|IV|i|passage=Let me but '''move''' one question to your daughter.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1630|author=w:John Hayward|title=The Life and Raigne of King Edward the Sixth |passage=And therefore they are to be blamed alike, both who moue and who decline warre{{...}}}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[mention]]; to raise (a question); to [[suggest]] (a course of action); to [[lodge]] (a complaint). #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:mention}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[incite]], [[urge]] (someone to do something); to [[solicit]] (someone for or of an issue); to make a proposal to. #: {{syn|en|motivate|provoke|Thesaurus:incite}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1485|author=Sir Thomas Malory|title=Le Morte Darthur|section=Book VII |passage="Sir," seyde Sir Boys, "ye nede nat to '''meve''' me of such maters, for well ye wote I woll do what I may to please you."}} #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=vii|page=40|passage=The thirſt of raigne and ſweetnes of a crowne, {{...}}
'''Moou’d''' me to menage armes againſt thy ſtate.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[apply]] to, as for [[aid]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Comedy of Errors|2|2|passage=To me she speaks; she '''moves''' me for her them}} # {{lbl|en|law|transitive|intransitive}} To [[request]] an [[action]] from the [[court]]. #: {{ux|en|An attorney '''moved''' the court to issue a restraining order.}} #: {{ux|en|The district attorney '''moved''' for a non-suit.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[bow]] or [[salute]] upon [[meet]]ing. # {{lb|en|transitive|business}} To [[sell]] or [[market]] (especially
